2026-09-16: high-feedback tail captures (Etherbunny range). Feedback map: Fb 46 -> 0.9194 and Fb 50 -> 0.9994. Fb 46 is the Depth-0 static capture fitted only where the tail is more than 50 dB above the noise floor (L 0.91944 +- 0.00001, R 0.91928; loosening the gate to 20 dB walks the answer up to 0.9199 because unsubtracted floor flattens the late decay -- gate the SNR, do not trust a long fit); an independent null scan of the whole tail peaks at 0.91944. Fb 50 is 0.99936 +- 0.0002, from the Depth-13 capture with the Depth-13 modulation loss (M = 0.9978 per pass, measured at Fb 46 on the same segment and range) divided out. The old map interpolated 40->0.8, 50->0.993 and gave 0.9158 at 46 -- 2.2 dB per 60 repeats too fast. NOTE the law: fb = Fb x 0.019987 fits BOTH new points to 0.00005 (0.919402 and 0.99936), i.e. the map is linear in Fb as always but tops out at 0.9994, not 1.0. The 10/25/40 points are left at 0.2/0.5/0.8 because that law puts them at 0.19987/0.49968/0.79949, differences of 0.0005 that their own 2026-09-14 captures could not resolve.

2026-09-16: NO fixed high damp in the loop. On the Depth-0 static capture the per-pass magnitude is flat from 500 Hz to 19 kHz within 0.03 dB (8k -0.701, 10k -0.703, 12k -0.696, 14k -0.702, 16k -0.699, 18k -0.696 dB/pass against -0.719 at 1 kHz); a one-pole at the app's quick-readout 12,895 Hz would cost -2.15 dB/pass at 18 kHz. blocks.damp_hz is explicitly null: do not add one. The HF loss the app fitted is the MODULATION (Depth 13 shows -1.54 dB/pass at 8 kHz at the same Fb 46 where Depth 0 shows -0.70), i.e. the interpolated read, which the engine's linear interp already produces.

2026-09-16: no level dependence and no saturation. Per-pass gain 0.9194-0.9209 over a 58 dB span of loop level (-26 to -84 dBFS at the output) with fit residuals of 0.001-0.02 dB/repeat; the loudest sample in any of the three captures is -12.84 dBFS, so the render_smod clip at +-1 never engages, and the 1 kHz tail at Fb 50 carries H2 -71.6 dBc / H3 -69.3 dBc at its loudest. The loop adds no measurable noise: after the Fb-46 tail dies the capture reads -90.9 dBFS against -90.7 dBFS in its own silence. That bounds the store at >= 14 bits; it cannot tell 16 from 18, so storage.bits stays 16.

2026-09-16: sample_rate 39057.15 -> 39055.79 (SUPERSEDED minutes later, see below). The Depth-0 Fb-46 tail capture measures the loop period at Dly 250 directly -- 249.642854 ms, repeat 1 against repeats 6/11/21/31, spread 4 ns, both channels -- and 9750/39055.79 is exactly that. The old rate was 0.31 device samples per repeat short, which over 112 repeats drifts 0.9 ms and holds the whole-tail null at -9.6 dB against -42.7 at the measured period. Like the 39057.15 it replaces this is a NULL-TEST constant, not a device clock: the unit is scope-confirmed at 39062.5 Hz and the plugin runs there. Only the product D/sample_rate is constrained by this capture -- 39063.81 with D=round(ms*39)+2 nulls at -40.6 dB, within 2 dB. See docs/smod-feedback-2026-09-16.md section 5a for the cross-evidence that the device law is D = round(ms*39)+2 at 39062.5 with the capture interface running 33.4 ppm slow.

2026-09-16 (reconciliation, same evening): sample_rate 39055.79 -> 39063.829787 (effective 153/188 of 48 kHz), maps.delay gained offset_samples: 2, adopting the SDLY/MODD/CHO clock (docs/sdly-clock-2026-09-16.md, 'Adopted 2026-09-16') in place of this file's own 9750-sample/no-offset fit. The two are the same law at two different measured rates: this capture's 249.642854 ms loop period is 9750 samples at 39055.79 Hz with NO offset, or 9752 samples (= round(250*39)+2) at 39063.83 Hz -- a 33 ppm rate difference the note above already flagged (39063.81 nulled the tail at -40.6 dB, 2 dB off the fitted rate's -42.7). Re-verified on the tail capture at the shared rate (tests/null_test.py, --signal capture/signalset-tail.wav --layout capture/layout-tail.json --eq out/null/chain-loop.npy --align-segment sine20): overall null -41.3/-41.2 dB L/R -- 1.4-1.5 dB short of the fitted-rate figure above (-42.7) and closer to the flagged 39063.81 test point (-40.6) than to the fitted 39055.79's own number, consistent with this rate being a shared-clock compromise across four models rather than this capture's own optimum. Not a regression from where this file stood minutes earlier (39055.79/no-offset was not independently re-verified here before being superseded) but recorded as the honest number rather than the assumed -43.8. SMOD Depth-0 normal-set capture unaffected (-32.9/-32.9 dB overall, identical to before this edit, insensitive to delay length by design -- see docs/sdly-clock-2026-09-16.md 'Other checks').
